entries.title: I Chronicles 26:1
segments: The porters; these had charge of the gates leading to the temple. The temple was not yet built in David's day, but the porters were assigned in anticipation of it; and their offices are here described as they existed under Solomon and onward.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:4
segments: Obed-edom; who took charge of the ark after the death of Uzzah.
Those who treat the ordinances of God with reverence, and are faithful in his service, may expect that he will prosper them and their children after them, and make them blessings to mankind.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:13
segments: In the service of God, each one should stand in his lot, and be ready to perform his portion of labor.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:20
segments: Of the Levites; these seem to have been Levites who were neither singers nor porters, but belonged to the twenty-four thousand who had charge of the work of the house of the Lord, having special services assigned to them connected with the sacred treasures.  This will explain the fact that so many of the names here mentioned are those contained in the list in

, while no name belonging to the singers or porters appears here. 
 
The treasures with which any one is intrusted should be guarded with care, and faithfully appropriated to the objects for which they are given.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:24
segments: The son of Gershom; that is, his descendant.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:25
segments: His brethren by Eliezer; Shebuel's brethren descended from Eliezer, who was also a son of Moses.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:27
segments: As all our treasures come from God, a suitable portion of them should be devoted to the support of his worship, and the spread of a knowledge of his truth and will throughout the world.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:28
segments: Whosoever had dedicated any thing; it had been customary for those who had property to dedicate a portion of it to the Lord.

entries.title: I Chronicles 26:29
segments: Of the Izharites; the sacred writer comes, in the last place, to notice the six thousand Levites who were officers and judges.
